statement: Salvage assessment for the X06.6 adoption: the dead worker's graph.rs hunk (adding procedural_records/route_traces Vecs + ingest_procedural/ingest_route_trace/procedural_records()/route_traces() accessors to MemoryGraph) and record.rs hunk (adding a Hash derive to RecordDomain) were both KEPT as-is, evaluated skeptically per the brief's caution that these files were consume-API-only in the dead worker's own scope. Both are genuinely minimal and necessary: observations.rs's record_procedural/record_route_choice literally call graph.ingest_procedural/ingest_route_trace and graph.procedural_records().len()/graph.route_traces().len(), so those accessors are load-bearing, not incidental scope creep; learning.rs's learning_curve builds HashMap<RecordDomain, Vec<LearningCurvePoint>>, which requires RecordDomain: Hash + Eq -- the single-line Hash derive is the only way to satisfy that without forking RecordDomain into a second type. Neither hunk changes existing MemoryGraph/RecordDomain behavior; both are strictly additive (new fields default-initialized via #[derive(Default)], new derive on an existing enum). graph.rs's own doc comment independently justifies keeping procedural/meta-memory in separate append-only Vecs rather than folding them into the MemoryNode enum: they are not recall-searchable text nodes and are a distinct specialized-memory kind per the owner intent's MIA-derived hierarchy (D-10) -- confirmed correct by a doctrine research pass over MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_BORROW_POLICY.md (MIA is "framework, translated", never a literal schema) and MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_DECISIONS.md D-10.
why: The brief specifically flagged graph.rs/record.rs as at-risk scope creep from a worker whose brief was consume-API-only, so a skeptical, load-bearing-vs-incidental review was required before keeping any hunk from a dead worker rather than rubber-stamping salvaged code.
howToApply: When adopting a dead worker's salvage that touches a file outside the adopting worker's own file claim, check whether the new code that DOES belong to the claim actually calls the touched file's new surface (grep for the accessor/derive's use sites) before keeping the hunk; keep only what is call-site-necessary and behavior-preserving, drop anything speculative or unused.

statement: The dead worker's salvaged code passed `cargo build -p enforcer-memory` and `cargo test -p enforcer-memory` cleanly at the salvage checkpoint, but `cargo clippy -p enforcer-memory --all-targets -- -D warnings` (which this workspace's Cargo.toml sets clippy::unwrap_used = "deny" and clippy::expect_used = "deny" for) caught 3 real violations confined entirely to learning.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module: two `.expect("...")` calls on Option::get(&RecordDomain) and one `.is_none()` check clippy flagged as unnecessary_get_then_check. None of these were in non-test code paths.
why: A prior worker died at a session limit after a plain `cargo build` passed, so the mandatory salvage-checkpoint commit in this lane's brief only required build-clean, not clippy-clean -- confirming clippy must be run as its own separate gate even when build+test are already green, because unwrap_used/expect_used denial is a clippy lint, not a compiler error.
howToApply: Never treat `cargo build`/`cargo test` passing as a proxy for `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` passing in this workspace; run clippy as an explicit, separate gate before every push, especially after adopting salvaged/foreign code that was only checked with `cargo build`.

statement: X06.6 continuous-learning acceptance surface (observation-per-operation-type, clean-scan negative evidence, recurrence-curve update after landing, lesson activation rules, supersede handling, route-choice trace with confidence, per-domain improvement curve) is fully covered by crates/enforcer-memory/tests/continuous_learning.rs (8 integration tests) against a dedicated fixture corpus (tests/fixtures/memory/continuous-learning.ndjson: 4 records spanning landed/superseded/unlanded lessons across the harness and code domains) that exercises the public API end to end (ingest_observation, evidence_chain/recurrence_curve, learning_curve/active_lessons/lesson_status/superseded_by, record_procedural/record_route_choice/procedural_success_rate, recall_pack) rather than re-deriving each module's own inline unit tests.
why: The workpack's hard-tests block names 7 requirements as a flat list without a 1:1 module mapping; writing one integration test per named requirement (plus a cross-cutting 8th proving the evidence-chain + SessionStart recall-pack contract together) makes the requirement-to-test mapping auditable without duplicating the 20+ inline unit tests each module already carries.
howToApply: When a workpack's hard-tests block lists requirements as prose rather than named test functions, write exactly one integration test per named requirement in a dedicated tests/<subpack>.rs file against a dedicated fixture, and keep each test's doc comment naming which hard-test number it satisfies so a reviewer can check off the acceptance block directly against the test file.

statement: ProceduralRecord and RouteTrace (X06.6 procedural/meta-memory) currently have no persistence path through crates/enforcer-memory/src/store/**'s AppendLog pattern -- they live only in MemoryGraph's in-memory Vecs and vanish on process exit, unlike Incident nodes (which flow through ingest_observation into the graph and, per X06.1, are intended to persist via the store's observation log). This is a known gap against D-02 ("truth lives in append-only logs; every index is derived and rebuildable") that store/** internals are explicitly out of this lane's file claim to fix.
why: Flagging this now (rather than silently shipping an in-memory-only procedural/meta-memory) matters because a future X06.7 (MCP/CLI) or X06.9 (parity/benchmark) worker consuming `memory evidence`/procedural success rates across a real session boundary would otherwise discover the data silently disappeared on restart, looking like a regression rather than a known, scoped-out gap.
howToApply: A future lane that owns crates/enforcer-memory/src/store/** should add a ProceduralLogEntry/RouteTraceLogEntry (or a unified ObservationLogEntry variant covering Incident+ProceduralRecord+RouteTrace) to src/schema.rs and wire it through Store's existing AppendLog<T> pattern (see Store::observation_log_mut/graph_event_log_mut for the precedent) so procedural/meta-memory survives a restart the same way Incident nodes are meant to.
